summary: Installed and loaded the S009 launchd scheduler (com.algo.s009-paper), which had never actually been running: no plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents, no launchd job, no cron entry -- since the last manual run on 2026-08-06 the paper ledger/state had gone stale (last_day stuck at 2026-08-05) while 4 real positions sat open on the dedicated Bybit-algo009 mainnet account with nothing auto-rebalancing them. Fixed a real bug this exposed in scripts/s009_tick.py: tick() defaulted its now parameter to timezone-aware UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)), but utils/trade_logger.py writes event timestamp fields as naive local time, so _has_event_today's since-cutoff comparison raised "can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes" on every idle tick once a heartbeat had already been logged for the day -- same failure signature as the two "S009 cycle subprocess exited non-zero" entries already in S009.log from 2026-08-03. Changed the default to naive local time (matching the logger and scripts/s007_tick.py's own default); this now parameter only affects heartbeat dedup/log-file day-naming, not the actual UTC trading-day boundary (_expected_last_closed_day() is independent of it). Added tests/scripts/test_s009_tick.py (regression test replays the exact two-consecutive-idle-ticks crash, plus branch coverage for the needs-cycle/timeout/nonzero-exit/state-did-not-advance paths, mirroring tests/scripts/test_s007_tick.py's structure). Per explicit user confirmation, also switched deployment/com.algo.s009-paper.plist from --broker off (shadow-only) to --broker execute --allow-mainnet, so the scheduler now auto-rebalances the real mainnet book daily; verified via BybitExec.positions()/wallet_equity() (read-only) that the reload itself placed no orders.

Added a shared Redis to the compose stack, reachable from every job-run worker container. docker-compose.yml: new redis service (redis:7.4.1-alpine, --appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec --maxmemory 512mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction, named volume redis-data, healthcheck redis-cli ping); new top-level network algo with an explicit name: algo (NOT project-prefixed) so the Ofelia job-run label can attach ephemeral worker containers -- which are created straight through the podman socket, not as compose services -- to it by literal name; added ofelia.job-run.dispatch.network: algo and REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379 to the job-run environment array; worker (build-only) service also put on algo for documentation. Redis is deliberately NOT published to the host (Anton chose internal-network-only, no auth): only compose containers reach it, a host process (the manually-run webapp) cannot -- utils/redis_client.is_available() returns False there. One instance serves two roles: STATE_DB=0 for durable shared state / distributed locks / pub-sub, CACHE_DB=1 for the market-data cache still parked in docs/DEV_PLANS.md (cache keys carry their own TTL; server is noeviction). New utils/redis_client.py: redis_url() (REDIS_URL env, else DEFAULT_REDIS_URL redis://redis:6379), lru_cached get_client(db, *, decode_responses) with 2s connect/op timeouts, never-raises is_available(); guards a missing redis package (in requirements-docker.txt, added redis==5.2.1; also requirements.txt redis>=5.2,<6). 4 tests in tests/utils/test_redis_client.py (URL resolution, is_available False+no-raise without a server). DEV_PLANS.md updated: replaced the deferred market-data-cache bullet with Shared-Redis + cache-infra-ready + scheduler-lock-migration-candidate bullets. NOT done: wiring get_m1 read-through, migrating scripts/scheduler_tick.py data/.scheduler_locks to a Redis lock. Worker image (algo-worker:latest) must be rebuilt to pick up the redis dependency. Not run live (podman machine not reachable from this session); compose YAML + label JSON arrays validated, full tests/utils green (18 passed).

Branch algodev-s011-stale-feed-and-ledger, commits dd81245 + b8f1b1d. (dd81245) Fixed the 2026-08-19 CAC40 oversizing: run_live_cycle_multi last_price now goes through CTraderS011._last_closed_price/_drop_forming_bar (forming-bar guard the RSI path already had). Fixes: new pure CTraderS011._session_dated_index (open_ts.ceil(D) UTC -> session date, DST/GMT-safe), _expected_last_closed_trading_date rewritten UTC-based vs new BROKER_DAY_CLOSE_UTC_HOUR=22, a stale-D1-feed guard in decide() that makes a genuinely-lagging-feed cycle a logged no-op (no orders/state/ledger, also throttles the ALGODEV-34 retry storm), run_cycle_for_account ledger_file:Path|None so the DB runner writes no ledger CSV (S009 2026-08-08 collision pattern), and scripts/s011_check_d1_alignment.py. ALGODEV-45 step 1: added scripts/s007_watchdog.py, a stateless detection-only watchdog for S007 (reads AccountStrategy.last_cycle_at, alerts to data/watchdog_alerts.log + events-<date>.jsonl if stale >3min during the trading window, never touches the broker or kills/restarts anything -- theres nothing persistent to manage yet). Scheduled every 2 minutes via deployment/schedule.ymls tasks: section, same Ofelia stateless-tick mechanism as everything else. Caught and fixed a real UTC-vs-local-time bug before deploy (compared UTC last_cycle_at against container-local datetime.now(), misjudging a healthy cycle as 180min stale -- exactly the Kyiv summer offset); fixed by keeping the pure logic in naive UTC and converting only the cron-window bounds to Europe/Kyiv. Verified two ways: (1) replayed the real 2026-09-16 Podman outage from this sessions own history through the logic as a regression test (one alert, no spam), (2) deployed live and confirmed silent+correct against the real DB. Deployed and running in production as of 2026-09-17 14:0x Kyiv.

Added an S021 cron entry (`* 16-23 * * 1-5`) to schedule.yml. Anton raised the DST-vs-timezone question directly: the project's Ofelia scheduler evaluates cron against the container's Europe/Kyiv wall clock (see docker-compose.yml TZ=Europe/Kyiv), so every existing schedule (S007/S009/S011) is written in Kyiv local time, not UTC -- that's a project-wide architecture fact, not something to special-case for one strategy. S021's own session anchor is fixed-EST (UTC-5, no DST -- passport sec 0/2), so in UTC it's a FIXED 14:30-20:59 window year-round; what still drifts is Kyiv's own DST shifting which *local* hour that UTC window falls on (16:30-22:59 Kyiv winter vs 17:30-23:59 Kyiv summer). Rather than hand-edit the cron line at each DST transition (the same unsolved problem already documented in this file for deribit_snapshot), used a wide 16:00-23:59 Kyiv window covering both seasons -- safe because bot/orb_signals.py::decide() derives "now" purely from the latest M1 bar's own (fixed-EST) timestamp, never the container's wall clock, so over-polling outside the true session is a cheap no-op, same principle as S007's own wide cron window. AccountStrategy.enabled stays False -- this only adds the schedule entry, doesn't turn anything on.

Superseded the wide Kyiv-window S021 cron entry added earlier today with an exact-UTC one, per Anton's explicit request to fix S021's scheduling properly rather than live with a padded-window workaround -- scoped deliberately to S021 only after showing that a full container TZ switch to UTC would touch already-live S009 (Bybit mainnet) / S011 (cTrader) schedules for no benefit and would force S007 onto a hand-maintained seasonal UTC offset in place of its current deliberate, zero-drift Kyiv/Frankfurt DST sync (see decisions-log.md 2026-09-22 for the full reasoning and the rejected alternatives). Added an optional per-entry `tz:` key to deployment/schedule.yml, implemented as scripts/scheduler_tick.py::_effective_now() (new CONTAINER_TZ = zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('Europe/Kyiv') constant) -- an entry with no `tz:` key is matched exactly as before (S007/S009/S011/watchdog/deribit_snapshot are completely unaffected), an entry with `tz: <IANA name>` gets `now` converted into that zone before croniter.match(). S021's entry changed from `* 16-23 * * 1-5` (Kyiv-local, wide) to `* 14-20 * * 1-5` + `tz: UTC` -- an exact, never-drifting mapping of its real fixed-EST session window (14:30-20:59 UTC year-round), no more DST padding needed. 6 new tests in tests/scripts/test_scheduler_tick.py (naive-datetime conversion for Kyiv winter/summer + passthrough, plus tick()-level integration proving a UTC-tz entry matches its own zone and not Kyiv's). Full existing suite (23/23) plus the wider tests/scripts/ + tests/webapp/test_runner_coordinator.py pass with no regressions (6 pre-existing, unrelated failures confirmed via git stash: a time-sensitive test_s007_tick.py assertion and 5 test_fetch_deribit_snapshot.py tests failing on missing fastparquet in this sandbox). AccountStrategy.enabled for S021 unchanged (still False) -- this is a scheduling-precision fix only.

Containerized the ALGODEV-45 step-2 S007 persistent-session observation daemon (scripts/s007_daemon.py) as a new docker-compose service "s007-daemon", per Anton's explicit request (manual `python -m scripts.s007_daemon` each time was not sustainable). Reuses the existing algo-worker:latest image (no new build), command overridden to `python -m scripts.s007_daemon --account-strategy-id 1`, restart: unless-stopped, same data/reports bind mounts and APP_SECRET_KEY/APP_DB_URL/TZ env as the Ofelia job-run workers. Unlike `worker` (build-only, profile-gated) this is a genuine standing service -- the daemon holds ONE long-lived cTrader session for hours by design, not a per-minute stateless tick, so it does not belong in deployment/schedule.yml (Ofelia's per-strategy CRON dispatch) or as another Ofelia job-run. `restart: unless-stopped` is a container-level restart (fresh process/session on exit), which does NOT contradict the script's own "no auto-reconnect by design" docstring invariant -- that note is about the in-process Twisted session never silently retrying mid-run, not about the daemon never coming back; updated that docstring to reflect the new deployment (still safe: read-only, never places an order, per its own SAFETY INVARIANT comment, unchanged). Verified live: `podman compose up -d s007-daemon` started cleanly, session came up, window-aware check correctly read active=True during the live 10:00-16:59 session, and its first tick saw n_positions=1, matching the real position the live trading path (webapp.runner -> _worker_s007) had just opened on the same account -- confirms it observes the same account without interfering.

Found live 2026-09-23: a Podman machine clock-drift heal (podman_healthcheck.py's existing `_heal()`) correctly restarted the machine and brought `ofelia` back up, but left the `s007-daemon` service (added earlier today as a standing compose service, see bot/deployment.jsonl same date) dead -- `machine stop` SIGKILLs every container in the VM and `machine start` does not auto-resume any of them, so only the one service `_heal()` explicitly ran `compose up -d` for (ofelia) came back. Real S007 trading resumed fine (ofelia dispatch unaffected), but s007-daemon sat `Exited (137)` for 8+ minutes with nothing bringing it back despite its own `restart: unless-stopped` (that policy only survives the CONTAINER exiting, not the whole VM being torn down). `redis` has the identical exposure (also not restarted by `_heal()`) -- turned out to not even be running at all before this incident (no `algo-redis-1` in `podman ps -a`, its `algo_redis-data` volume didn't exist yet either), though that had no trading impact since Redis is guarded as an optional accelerator everywhere it's used. Fixed: generalized `_heal()`'s single ofelia compose-up into a `HEAL_SERVICES = ("ofelia", "redis", "s007-daemon")` loop (ofelia first, since only it gates real trading and keeps its own dedicated retry block); `_ofelia_running()` refactored into a name-parameterized `_service_running()` helper reused for the other two. The final "healed" event now also requires `other_services_ok` (redis + s007-daemon both running), not just ofelia+clock, logging which service(s) specifically failed to come back otherwise. Manually brought both back up live via `podman compose up -d redis s007-daemon` (redis's volume now exists) -- verified all three running, S007-daemon resumed clean ticks, real S007 trading resumed at 14:13 after an ~8min gap (14:05-14:13, no missed orders -- day was already risk-capped through that window). Updated test_ofelia_not_running_after_first_compose_triggers_retry's expected compose-call count from a hardcoded 2 to `len(hc.HEAL_SERVICES) + 1` so it doesn't need touching again if HEAL_SERVICES grows. Full suite: 11/13 pass; the other 2 failures (test_link_never_run_past_grace_period_is_stale, test_link_with_old_cycle_is_stale_existing_behavior_preserved) are pre-existing and unrelated -- a hardcoded now=datetime(2026,9,22,...) fixture racing the real wall-clock date (now 2026-09-23) used internally by StrategyLogger's own events-<date>.jsonl filename, confirmed unrelated to this change (both call only _check_daily_strategy_freshness, never touched here).

Two fixes for the 2026-09-24 S021 overnight-position incident (see this session's earlier entry on the incident itself), per Anton's explicit 2-part request: '1: закрывать позы на 10 минут раньше, 2: каждое утро проверять позы по ТС и закрывать если что-то пошло не так'. (1) bot/orb_config.py: added LIVE_EXIT_BUFFER_MIN=10 -- decide()'s live time-exit check (bot/orb_signals.py, case 3/4) now fires 10 minutes before strategies.orb_intraday.config::ORB_BASE.session_close (15:59 fixed-EST) instead of AT it, giving the cron window (ends 20:59 UTC = 15:59 fixed-EST) 10 one-minute cycles of slack to actually catch and execute the close instead of 0 (the exact gap that caused yesterday's incident: the last cycle of the day was 2 minutes short). Deliberately does NOT touch session_close itself -- that field is also read by the frozen backtest engine (strategies/orb_intraday/engine.py) and by decide()'s own ADR-session-validity threshold, neither of which should move (strategy-passport-S021.md sec 10: 'не переоптимизировать') -- this is a live-only operational safety margin, computed in minutes (no new datetime imports needed). 19/19 tests/bot/test_orb_*.py pass unchanged. (2) New scripts/position_audit.py: reads every open broker position via the existing CTraderS007/CTraderORB.open_positions()/close_position() methods (no new order-sending code -- reuses the same path the live strategies already use) and closes anything still open, for S007 (account_strategy id=1) and S021 (id=5) only -- explicitly rejects S009/S011 (SystemExit) since those are multi-day/portfolio strategies where an open position before session start is the NORMAL resting state, not a defect. Relies on a timing invariant instead of per-strategy timezone/date arithmetic: scheduled to run 5 minutes BEFORE each strategy's own session opens (see deployment/schedule.yml's two new task entries, s007_position_audit at 09:55 Kyiv and s021_position_audit at 13:55 UTC via tz:UTC), so 'any position still open at audit time' is stale by construction -- no label/date parsing needed, which sidesteps S007 (Europe/Bucharest-anchored labels) vs S021 (fixed UTC-5-anchored labels) using different date references. 4 new tests (tests/scripts/test_position_audit.py, DB and adapter classes monkeypatched, no real broker/DB touched): scope-guard rejection, clean state closes nothing, a stale S021 position gets closed, S007 uses the right adapter class. algo-worker:latest rebuilt (`podman compose build worker`) so both the exit-buffer fix and the new audit task are live from the next scheduled tick -- verified via full test suite (scheduler_tick + bot: 147/147 pass) before the rebuild.
